title: A warm cache is not permission
description: Paid video segments should share cached bytes across viewers. A valid signed URL warms the cache, but a later request with an expired signature still receives the segment because signature checks run only on a cache miss. Which design closes the gap without creating one cached copy per viewer?

options.text: Put the signature and expiry in the cache key and validate only misses.
options.explanation: This fragments the cache and still lets a previously cached URL work after its expiry if hits bypass validation.

options.text: Ask the origin to check entitlement only when an object is first cached.
options.explanation: Authorization for one fetch does not authorize later viewers. A warm object cannot stand in for per-request validation.

options.text: Stop caching private segments and proxy every request to the origin.
options.explanation: Origin authorization could be made safe, but abandoning caching is unnecessary and loses the required shared-byte delivery benefit.

options.text: Validate signature and expiry on every request before cache lookup, then exclude validated signing parameters from the cache key.
options.explanation: Every viewer must pass the access check, even on a hit. Authorized requests can then share one cached segment because the signing parameters do not change its bytes.
